title: SMB: Numerous fixes and enhancements for SMB1/SMB2 dissection
description: This pull request contains a collection of numerous fixes and enhancements for both the SMB1 and SMB2 protocol dissectors. Changes include correcting non-UNICODE string parsing, fixing UTIME dissection, improving error code display, and updating the dissection of NTLMSSP access masks and security descriptors.

This is wrong, please revert.  See

https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/windows_protocols/ms-nlmp/b34032e5-3aae-4bc6-84c3-c6d80eadf7f2

            DomainName ... MUST be encoded using the OEM character set.
            WorkstationName ... MUST be encoded using the OEM character set.

https://davenport.sourceforge.net/ntlm.html#theType1Message

            The supplied domain ... is always in OEM format, even if Unicode is supported by the client.
            The supplied workstation ... too, is in OEM rather than Unicode.
    
Note too that the flags are known as NTLMSSP_NEGOTIATE_OEM_DOMAIN_SUPPLIED
and NTLMSSP_NEGOTIATE_OEM_WORKSTATION_SUPPLIED.

This causes a malformed error in frame 4 of map_cap_interesting.pcap in !10193
The other parts may well be correct, so I can revert just the flawed part of NTLMSSP NEGOTIATE and add a comment.

Real SMB2 communications have shown that it behaves the way the commit handles it, but we can't find the pcaps confirming it, so it's possible that it behaves that way only under some specific circumstances. Revert that one commit if you want, I can't argue when I don't have evidence.

The sample pcap in !10193 does have the client Unicode bit set but, as documented, sends the domain and workstation name in the OEM character set. I would be very interested in seeing any samples with other behavior that is unfortunately contrary to Microsoft's published specification if you can find them.

Our attempts to reproduce it now failed. Originally, it looked like Windows' SMB2 implementation didn't match the documentation (which isn't uncommon). Feel free to revert it, but it might help if there was a unit test to check that it can work with your pcap correctly.

I agree that it's not uncommon. Sometimes we then have a difficult choice between dissecting according to the specification and calling real world practice an error or accommodating the real world practice. Please let us know if you can find an example.
No, we looked for it and we found nothing, and attempts to replicate that scenario where this field is used were unsuccessful.

commits_data.title: SMB: Fix parsing SMB1 non-UNICODE fixed length strings
commits_data.message:
SMB: Fix parsing SMB1 non-UNICODE fixed length strings

In most cases non-UNICODE fixed length strings in SMB1 packets have
terminating null byte, similarly to UNICODE strings which have terminating
null wide-character.

So do not replace terminating null byte by UNICODE replacement character in
every non-UNICODE fixed length strings in SMB1 packets when dissecting
them.

commits_data.title: SMB: Fix dissecting SMB1 UTIME
commits_data.message:
SMB: Fix dissecting SMB1 UTIME

SMB1 UTIME value 0xffffffff is special only for SMB1 close command. It
means to not change time value at all. But for all other commands it may be
valid timestamp, depending on server behavior. For example it is valid on
Windows 98 SMB server.

SMB1 UTIME value 0x00000000 has special meaning for every SMB1 command.
Meaning differs between commands. In all responses it means that server did
not provide this time value (e.g. because it does not know it). For create
file requests or writeandclose requests it means to use current server
time. And in close and setinfo requests it means to not change time at all.

Fix dissect_smb_UTIME() function to correctly dissect special values
0xffffffff and 0x00000000 and use supplied human readable descriptions from
each SMB command.

SMB: Dissect SMB1 NT IOCTL Setup response

It contains one 16-bit word which is the original non-truncated IOCTL
response output data buffer length.

commits_data.title: SMB: Show NTLMSSP empty username as anonymous
commits_data.message:
SMB: Show NTLMSSP empty username as anonymous

Currently Empty username in NTLMSSP Session Setup Request is showed as "\".

Empty username in NTLM Session Setup Request is already showed as
"anonymous". Do same thing for NTLMSSP Session Setup Request.

commits_data.title: SMB: Primary Domain in SMB1 Lanman Negotiate is always in ASCII
commits_data.message:
SMB: Primary Domain in SMB1 Lanman Negotiate is always in ASCII

SMB1 LAN Manager dialects do not support UNICODE. So Primary Domain in SMB1
Lanman Negotiate response cannot be in UNICODE even if Unicode Strings flag
is set in header.

Checked against Windows Server 2022 which for LAN Manager dialects sends
Primary Domain in ASCII, but copies header flags from request. So if the
request has Unicode Strings flag set, it is present also in response.

commits_data.title: SMB: Fix dissecting of Negotiate cryptkey from LAN Manager 1.x and 2.0 dialects
commits_data.message:
SMB: Fix dissecting of Negotiate cryptkey from LAN Manager 1.x and 2.0 dialects

LAN Manager 1.x and 2.0 dialects do not use Encryption key (challenge)
length field (chl). In these dialects is that field always zero. The real
length of Negotiate cryptkey for these dialects is stored in byte count
field. These dialects do not have Primary domain field.

Distinguish between LAN Manager 1.x/2.0 (which do not have Primary domain
field) and LAN Manager 2.1 (which has optional Primary domain field) via
the Encryption key (challenge) length field (chl).

And properly dissect cryptkey from LAN Manager 1.x and 2.0 dialects which
have zero in chl.

commits_data.title: SMB: Add comments about CorePlus dialect into dissect_negprot_response()
commits_data.message:
SMB: Add comments about CorePlus dialect into dissect_negprot_response()

Word Count == 13 in SMB1 Negotiate Response indicates also CorePlus dialect.

commits_data.title: SMB: Recognize SMB1 DOS error code 52 (0x34)
commits_data.message:
SMB: Recognize SMB1 DOS error code 52 (0x34)

Windows SMB1 server for SMB TreeConnectAndX message returns NT status code
STATUS_DUPLICATE_NAME (0xc00000bd) or DOS error code 52 (0x34) when
hostname part of Path does not match server's its own hostname.

DOS error code 52 (0x34) in MS-DOS is formatted as "Duplicate name on network".

commits_data.title: SMB: Fix displaying SMB1 non-NT status codes
commits_data.message:
SMB: Fix displaying SMB1 non-NT status codes

Function proto_tree_add_uint_format_value() does not print error code
itself, so print error code by additional format argument.

To prevent showing unknown error codes two times (once by additional
argument in proto_tree_add_uint_format_value() and second time by
val_to_str_ext() called in decode_smb_error()), change logic in
decode_smb_error() function to show unknown error codes conditionally
specified by additional function argument.

Prefix all hex error codes by "0x" string, so it would be unambiguous that
error codes are printed in hex format.

And fix decode_smb_error() function to format unknown error codes also for
SMB_SUCCESS class and unknown classes.

commits_data.title: SMB: File name in SMB1 SMB_FILE_NAME_INFO response is always in UNICODE
commits_data.message:
SMB: File name in SMB1 SMB_FILE_NAME_INFO response is always in UNICODE

MS-CIFS 2.2.8.3.9 SMB_QUERY_FILE_NAME_INFO and then also MS-CIFS 2.2.8.3.11
SMB_QUERY_FILE_ALT_NAME_INFO explicitly mention that FileName is of WCHAR
array type. WCHAR type always means UNICODE, also when running under
non-UNICODE session.

So always decode File name from SMB_FILE_NAME_INFO and
SMB_FILE_ALT_NAME_INFO responses as UNICODE string.

commits_data.title: SMB: File name in SMB1 SMB_FILE_ALL_INFO response is always in UNICODE
commits_data.message:
SMB: File name in SMB1 SMB_FILE_ALL_INFO response is always in UNICODE

MS-CIFS 2.2.8.3.10 SMB_QUERY_FILE_ALL_INFO explicitly mention that FileName
is of WCHAR array type. WCHAR type always means UNICODE, also when running
under non-UNICODE session.

So always decode File name from SMB_FILE_ALL_INFO response as UNICODE
string.

Checked against Windows SMB server (from Windows Server 2022) and also
Samba server. Both return this FileName field in UNICODE, even in
non-UNICODE session.

commits_data.title: SMB: Update comment about REPARSE_TAG_AF_UNIX
commits_data.message:
SMB: Update comment about REPARSE_TAG_AF_UNIX

REPARSE_TAG_AF_UNIX is used by both WinAPI and WSL. It was introduced for
WinAPI/Winsock [1] and later for WSL [2].

[1] - https://devblogs.microsoft.com/commandline/af_unix-comes-to-windows/
[2] - https://devblogs.microsoft.com/commandline/windowswsl-interop-with-af_unix/

commits_data.message:

commits_data.title: Fix NT/SMB Security Descriptor control bit description
commits_data.message:
Fix NT/SMB Security Descriptor control bit description

Server Security affects only DACL, so add DACL prefix like for all other
DACL control bits of Security Descriptor.

commits_data.title: SMB: Dissect NT/SMB/Windows access mask constant 0x01000000
commits_data.message:
SMB: Dissect NT/SMB/Windows access mask constant 0x01000000

Access mask constant 0x01000000 (SYSTEM_SECURITY_ACCESS) is in SACL ACE
list for auditing or alarming access to SACL itself.

commits_data.title: SMB: Remove NT/SMB/Windows access mask constant 0x00800000
commits_data.message:
SMB: Remove NT/SMB/Windows access mask constant 0x00800000

Access mask constant 0x00800000 is not used by NT, SMB or Windows systems
for anything. It does not gain access to SACLs.
